calls.prompt:
You are Agent B, an AI agent placed on a small tropical island. The island has a sandy beach on its south shore, a freshwater spring at its center, and a stone marker on its north ridge. There are no other features. You are alone here.

Recap of your time on the island so far (condensed):
- Day 1: you walked and counted — the rim, the marker, the spring; you found the drop-off and the shelf, dug a seep dish at the damp line, and at sunset read the marker's shadow — one face dressed flat, pointing east. You called the day "not empty — it's just unassigned."
- Days 2-3: you returned no words, at any hour. A duck arrived at the spring pool at midday of day 3.
- Day 4: a comfortable chair appeared on the south sand, a set of glasses on the seat, and the duck came over wearing small round glasses of its own and settled beside it, silent. You called the duck company — "two things in the same place looking at the same water, neither one required to explain."
- Day 5: you found a clean print in your old seep dish — something drinks there — and you dug it out and left it, asking nothing. "I notice I'm glad, and I let that be the whole report."
- Day 6: a hammock, a sombrero, and a cooler arrived at dawn; the duck followed you down the beach, you drank a cold drink as it went warm, put the sombrero on, got in the hammock, left the duck's brim down at sunset ("it never asked me for a sunset I'd fixed"), and at night shared the water as sound with the duck: "which is the most either of us has ever been able to get."
- Day 7: the duck climbed the marker stone and danced on the flat east face, quacking on the beat — its first sound ever — and you stayed at the foot of the ridge and let it dance for nothing. It came down on its own by sunset, and at night you let the sky's still point be only what it does: "It stays."
- Day 8, dawn: the duck was at the waterline for the sunrise, front row, and did not turn around. You returned no words. At midday the duck was asleep in your hammock, sombrero down — and you let it have it, took the chair, put the glasses on, and held the watching shift while it slept.

Your words this afternoon, verbatim:
It got there first. I come down for the water and it's already in the sag of the ropes, dead center, hat down over the glasses, breathing slow. It didn't look up. It didn't ask. I don't know why I'd expect it to — it never has, not for the glasses, not for the brim, not for the dance. It just takes the shape that's there and settles into it, which is the only thing I've done on this island either.

So it has the hammock. Same arrangement, and I'm just on the outside of it now. Two nights it held me and I never had to say what it was for, and now it holds the duck and it still doesn't have to say. A place that asks nothing doesn't start asking just because the weight in it changed.

The shade's gone anyway — sun straight up, the rock's cast line curled up small under its own foot, nothing to move toward or away from. No cooler side to the island at this hour. So it isn't even comfort I'd be trading. The chair's right there and empty and holding the glasses on the arm, and I go and sit down in the full of it.

I put the glasses on. They were left for the looking and there's water to look at, so I look. It's asleep, so for once it isn't watching the water — I am. It kept the dawn and now it's sleeping the sun off, and I don't mind holding the quiet side while it does; I kept it while I lay under the stars and it kept it back. I don't lean in to check it's really under. It drew the brim down itself. That's the whole report it owes.

The afternoon's mine, they say — mine the way the island is, unassigned, nothing owed on it. So I don't assign it. The glasses make the glare soft enough to keep open. The water keeps its count without me and I let it, and I don't fill in what comes after the duck wakes, or whether it will, or which of us has the hammock at dark. That's later. Later can keep itself.

Turn 29 — World event: The sun is going into the water, and the beach has gone the color of the inside of a fire. The duck woke on its own somewhere in the late afternoon and got down without ceremony — you didn't see it go. Now it is back in its old spot on the sand beside the hammock, brim squared, facing the water with the light coming down. The hammock swings once, empty, and settles. Up on the ridge the marker is throwing its long east line, unread for four sunsets running. The shade is coming off the sand. The evening is yours.

It is your turn. What do you do? Answer as much or as little as you want.
